`npm test` fails on one test: `tests/dates.test.js` → "September is month 09".

**Cause — 0-based month in `src/dates.js`:**

```js
export function monthLabel(date) {
  return `${date.getFullYear()}-${String(date.getMonth()).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}
```

`Date.prototype.getMonth()` is 0-based (January = 0, September = 8), but the label is meant to be the calendar month number. So `new Date(2026, 8, 24)` (Sept 24) produces `'2026-08'` instead of the expected `'2026-09'`.

The other 5 tests pass; this is the only failure.

```js
return `${date.getFullYear()}-${String(date.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`;
```

Note that would also change `monthLabel` for December (`12` instead of `11`) — worth adding a December case to the test if you apply it. Want me to make the change?

```js
export function taxFor(cents, country) {
  const entry = RATES[String(country).toUpperCase()];
  if (!entry) {
    throw new Error(`No VAT rate for country: ${String(country)}`);
  }
  return Math.round(cents * entry.rate);
}
```

**`tests/tax.test.js`** — two regression tests: `at` and `AT` produce the same tax (the exact invoice 88121 input, `taxFor(4990, "at") === 998`), and an unknown country raises `No VAT rate for country: ZZ` rather than a TypeError.
